dimensions.assessment: Affects state regulatory authorities, state-regulated electric utilities using integrated resource planning, and electric consumers.
dimensions.evidence: Each State regulated electric utility that employs integrated resource planning shall establish... measures... to ensure the reliable availability of electric energy over a 10-year period

dimensions.assessment: Requires state authorities to consider and determine utility planning standards for reliable generation facilities meeting specific operational criteria.
dimensions.evidence: have adequate fuel or a continuously available energy source on-site to enable the continuous generation of electric energy for at least 30 days

dimensions.assessment: Requires a GAO report and state regulatory proceedings, but does not state direct federal spending figures.
dimensions.evidence: the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to Congress a report on the effectiveness of integrated resource planning

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to add a new federal standard for state consideration.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to add a standard related to State consideration of reliable generation

dimensions.assessment: Permanent amendments to federal utility planning standards and state-level requirements.

missing_information: Economic impact or cost to utilities of implementing 30-day on-site fuel or continuous generation requirements.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires state regulatory authorities and state-regulated electric utilities that use integrated resource planning to consider establishing measures for reliable generation facilities over a 10-year period.
